sources.citation: Breen, Gavan. 2016. What's up with /u/. In Peter K. Austin, Harold Koch & Jane Simpson (eds), Language, land & song: Studies in honour of Luise Hercus, 158-171. London: EL Publishing. ISBN 978-0-728-60406-3.
sources.note: Phonology content relevant to Guyambal is one line (p. 165, sec. 4.2): the alternation Gujambal ~ Kwiambal is cited as an instance of /kuya-/ heard as [kwia-]. The chapter's general remark that stress in Australian languages 'is typically on the first syllable' and 'can move to a later syllable if that syllable has a long or a low' vowel (pp. 161-162) is about Australian languages at large (Arandic, Nganyaywana, Mbabaram), not a statement about Guyambal; nothing on Guyambal stress or tone.
